items.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: There’s only one, two, three — about three of us, four of us, Johnny Grimes, great trumpet player; Doris Rollin, one of the singers

ctx.x: The next band was organized by one of Benny Goodman’s saxophone players called Jerry Jerome. And he’s still living God rest his — he’s almost 90 years old, he’s living in the south somewhere. But myself, John Simmons on bass, I can’t think of the piano player’s name, and Arthur Herbert on drums, we were the first band, integrated band to play at Kelly’s Stables on 52nd Street. And one night, a great pianist named Nat Jaffe, said, “Hey man, this is one heck of a band, why don’t we keep this thing together?” And we…
Was there certain parts of the country that were worse than others as far as race?
